## Motivation

Some deployments need a machine-readable signal that text was generated by an AI system, including provenance workflows and transparency obligations such as [Article 50 of the EU AI Act](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj/eng). This PR adds opt-in text watermarking to sampled generation without adding tokens or changing default serving behavior.

## What this PR adds

- Keyed Aaronson-Gumbel sampling over the post-penalty, grammar-masked, top-k/top-p/min-p distribution, with model-free Gamma-test detection from token IDs.
- Returned logprobs reflect the pre-watermark target distribution (the sampler computes them from the unforced distribution when `return_logprob` is set, matching the speculative-decode semantic).
- Server configuration through `--enable-watermark` plus one `--watermark-config` JSON object, given as a file path or inline (`key`, `key_b`, `context_window`, `mixing_probability`, `max_probability`, `default_enabled`, `enforce_all`), with explicit opt-in, default-on, and enforce-all policy modes and secret redaction.
- Per-request enablement, keys, and context windows, including mixed watermarked and unwatermarked batches.
- Opt-in dual-key selection with a deterministic per-context coin and matching detector views; single-key behavior is unchanged when key B is absent.
- Verified normal decode plus NGRAM, EAGLE, EAGLE3, and NEXTN, including TP2/TP4 and DP2/TP2 normal/NEXTN service gates.
- An in-tree `WatermarkDetector` that also works as a copied package without SGLang or PyTorch, plus a reference HTTP detection server that uses the same `--watermark-config`.
- Repeated-context loop prevention, greedy bypass, fused normal/speculative state kernels, and a host-gated path that launches no watermark kernels for fully disabled batches.
- Fail-closed admission for unsupported modes, including DFLASH/DSPARK, pipeline-parallel speculation, rejection-sampling speculation, beam search, PD disaggregation, custom logit processors, and non-CUDA devices.

## Performance and evidence

Relative results are within-engine ON/OFF comparisons. Finite-top-k and speculative rows use random 1,024/512 requests, c8, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, 10 warmups, 100 measured requests, and three repetitions unless noted.

| Workload | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B, GSM8K-100 (sgl-eval) | 95-97% accuracy / 100% stop across normal decode (B200), NGRAM with `--disable-overlap-schedule` (H200), and EAGLE3; detection ON p=`1.09e-20` to `4.18e-27`, OFF p=`0.325-0.995`; greedy stopped safely in every gate |
| Qwen3-8B H200, no spec, finite top-k, c1 / c8 | Output throughput `+0.13% / +0.02%` (run-to-run noise) |
| Qwen3-8B GB300, no spec, unlimited top-k, c8 | `224.88 → 212.84` output tok/s per stream (`−5.35%`) |
| Qwen3.5-9B GB300 TP2, NEXTN 3/1/4 | TPOT `2.246 → 2.451 ms` (`+9.17%`); final-head same-pair spot check `+8.92%` |
| Capability enabled, fully disabled EAGLE3 traffic | TPOT `2.465 → 2.469 ms` versus merge-base (`+0.14%`) |
| Dual key versus single key, GB300 | Output throughput `−0.21%` c1 / `−1.50%` c8, within repetition variance |
| Speculative accept length | `2.759 → 2.783` (`+0.85%`) |

The DP2/TP2 gate used Qwen3-8B on two H200 GPUs: GSM8K-100 was 95% with 100% stop, both ranks detected at p=`1.84e-23`, disabled controls were p=`0.358`, repeated one-rank-idle batches remained healthy, and a DP2/TP2 NEXTN smoke detected at p=`2.14e-36` on both ranks.

## Cross-engine reference

Compare each engine's within-engine ON/OFF delta rather than absolute throughput.

| Workload | SGLang | vLLM nightly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-9B MTP, TP2 GB300, c8, top-k 20 | TPOT `+9.17%`; accept length `+0.85%` | `dual_key_gumbel`: TPOT `+14.24%`; accept length `+0.72%` |
| Qwen3-8B H200, no spec, top-k 20, c1 / c8 | Output throughput `+0.13% / +0.02%` | Plain Gumbel: `−1.70% / −2.11%` |

## Limitations

- Temperature 0 carries no signal. Short or low-entropy spans are weaker, and `max_probability` trades signal for ordinary sampling at low-entropy positions.
- Paraphrase and translation erase the signal; edits reduce the number of usable contexts.
- Murmur32 is a keyed, non-cryptographic mix. Key holders can both detect and forge; inline `--watermark-config` JSON is process-visible, and core dumps may contain in-memory keys.
- Unlimited top-k requires a full-vocabulary sort and measured `−2.8%` to `−7.2%` per-stream throughput; finite `top_k=20` was within noise. Unlimited-top-k speculative verification uses the slower tensor path.
- Watermarking stops after `min(4,096, per-request token-pool capacity)` admitted contexts. Runtime uses 32-bit context-hash admission while the detector deduplicates exact tuples; rare collisions and conservative sibling suppression only dilute signal.
- Speculative cost and acceptance are model- and workload-dependent, especially for top-k-1 draft chains, although the public NEXTN/EAGLE3 measurements above preserved acceptance.

The in-tree [`watermarking/README.md`](https://github.com/JustinTong0323/sglang/blob/watermark/python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking/README.md) is the design reference. Evaluation results remain in **Performance and evidence** and **Cross-engine reference** above. Configuration, request semantics, the normative detector contract, standalone use, and the compatibility matrix are in the [`text_watermarking.mdx` operator guide](https://github.com/JustinTong0323/sglang/blob/watermark/docs/docs/advanced_features/text_watermarking.mdx).

Co-authored-by: Nihar Patel <nihpat95@gmail.com>

## Test plan

CUDA selector/state parity suites, OpenAI endpoint e2e, the Rust `wire.rs` schema test, registry entries in `test_parity.py` and `test_model_overrides.py`, full changed-file pre-commit/taxonomy checks, and public-model GSM8K/detection/greedy/speculative/TP/DP service gates.

@@ -0,0 +1,391 @@
+---
+title: "Text Watermarking"
+metatags:
+    description: "Configure Aaronson-Gumbel text watermarking and detect watermarked text."
+---
+
+SGLang provides opt-in Aaronson-Gumbel watermarking for sampled text. The watermark replaces random token selection with a keyed, deterministic choice that follows the same output distribution under the ideal independent-uniform hash model, so anyone holding the secret key can later test whether a token sequence carries the watermark. Detection needs only the key and the token IDs; it does not need the model or a GPU.
+
+This feature can support transparency controls such as the machine-readable marking and detectability described in [Article 50 of the EU AI Act](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj). It is one technical signal, not a complete compliance program or proof of authorship.
+
+## How it works
+
+### Generation
+
+At each sampling step, SGLang first applies frequency, presence, and repetition penalties, logit bias, and any structured-output grammar mask, followed by the request's temperature and its top-k, top-p, and min-p truncation, then renormalizes. Let `p_i` be the resulting probability of candidate token `i`; grammar-masked and truncated tokens have `p_i = 0` and can never be selected. For each candidate, SGLang hashes the key, the preceding token context, and the token ID into a uniform value `u_i` in `(0, 1)` and selects
+
+```text
+argmax over i with p_i > 0 of  log(u_i) / p_i
+```
+
+When the `u_i` are independent uniforms, this rule selects token `i` with probability exactly `p_i`, so a single step is distributed like ordinary sampling. Ties go to the lowest token ID.
+
+A position is watermarked only when all of the following hold; otherwise the request samples that position normally:
+
+- The request has watermarking enabled (see [Per-request control](#per-request-control)).
+- The request is not greedy. `temperature=0` is normalized to `top_k=1`, and `top_k=1` positions are never watermarked.
+- The context is not empty.
+- The context has not already been watermarked earlier in the same request. Runtime identifies a context by its 32-bit context hash.
+- The request has watermarked fewer than `min(4,096, per-request token-pool capacity)` contexts.
+- The largest truncated probability is at most the server's `max_probability`. The default `1.0` disables this gate.
+
+Only a watermarked position enters the request's context history. A position skipped by the probability gate therefore leaves its context eligible for a later, higher-entropy occurrence, and once a request reaches its context budget the remaining tokens use ordinary sampling. The repeated-context rule keeps a repeated context from forcing the same token indefinitely.
+
+The context for a position is the last `h` tokens before it, where `h` is the request's context window, taken from the prompt followed by the tokens generated so far. The first generated token therefore uses the last `h` prompt tokens. A context is shorter than `h` only when fewer than `h` tokens precede the position.
+
+### Hash contract
+
+All arithmetic wraps to unsigned 32 bits. The primitives are the MurmurHash3 x86 32-bit body mix and finalizer:
+
+```text
+mix(state, value):
+  value = value * 0xcc9e2d51
+  value = rotl32(value, 15)
+  value = value * 0x1b873593
+  state = rotl32(state XOR value, 13)
+  return state * 5 + 0xe6546b64
+
+fmix32(value):
+  value = value XOR (value >> 16)
+  value = value * 0x85ebca6b
+  value = value XOR (value >> 13)
+  value = value * 0xc2b2ae35
+  return value XOR (value >> 16)
+```
+
+A key is 1 to 16 hexadecimal digits with an optional `0x` prefix, interpreted as an unsigned 64-bit integer; `key_lo` and `key_hi` are its low and high 32-bit words. For a context of `L` token IDs `c_1 ... c_L` and a candidate token `t`:
+
+```text
+context_hash = fmix32(mix(...mix(mix(0, c_1), c_2)..., c_L) XOR (4 * L))
+token_hash   = fmix32(mix(mix(mix(mix(0, key_lo), key_hi), context_hash), t) XOR 16)
+u            = (token_hash + 0.5) / 2^32
+```
+
+The context hash covers only the context tokens; keys enter only through the token hash and, in dual-key mode, through a per-context coin that chooses which key produces the token hash:
+
+```text
+coin      = fmix32(mix(mix(mix(mix(mix(0, a_lo), a_hi), b_lo), b_hi), context_hash) XOR 20)
+threshold = floor(P * 2^32)
+key       = key A if coin < threshold else key B
+```
+
+`a_lo`/`a_hi` and `b_lo`/`b_hi` are the words of key A and key B, and `P` is the server's `mixing_probability`.
+
+### Detection
+
+A detector holding the key scores each generated token `t` with `s = -log(1 - u)`, where `u` comes from the hash contract above using that token's context. Without the watermark, each `s` is an independent `Exponential(1)` sample. With the watermark, the generator preferred tokens with large `u`, so the scores are inflated.
+
+Over `n` scored contexts, the score `S = sum(s)` follows `Gamma(shape=n, scale=1)` under the null hypothesis that the text is not watermarked with this key. The detector reports the upper-tail probability `P[Gamma(n, 1) >= S]` as the p-value, its natural logarithm (finite even when the p-value underflows to `0.0`), and the normal approximation `z = (S - n) / sqrt(n)`.
+
+To match generation, a detector must follow these rules:
+
+1. Use the exact prompt token IDs that preceded the completion and the request's context window `h`. With prompt IDs, the first completion token's context is the last `h` prompt tokens. Without prompt IDs, the first `h` completion tokens have unknown contexts and are skipped.
+2. Score each distinct context once. The detector compares exact context token tuples, whereas generation compares 32-bit context hashes. After a hash collision, generation skips a later distinct context that the detector still scores. That extra score is an ordinary null sample, so the mismatch can only weaken detection, never create evidence.
+3. Stop after the generation request's context budget and report a prefix test. The default detector budget is 4,096 distinct contexts. If the server's per-request token-pool capacity is lower, pass that lower value as `max_contexts`; scoring the unforced tail adds null samples that dilute the statistic without adding evidence. With a maximum-probability gate below `1.0`, the model-free detector cannot identify skipped positions, so this fixed prefix is conservative and may omit signal from later forced positions.
+
+Positions that generation left unforced (greedy positions, and positions skipped by `max_probability`) are indistinguishable from ordinary text to the detector, which scores them as null samples; they dilute the statistic but cannot produce false evidence.
+
+A low p-value is evidence that the text carries the keyed watermark. It is not a calibrated probability that a particular author or model produced the text. Applications must choose a decision threshold and measure false-positive and false-negative rates on their own traffic.
+
+## Server configuration
+
+`--enable-watermark` turns the feature on; every other watermark setting lives in one JSON object passed with `--watermark-config`, either as a file path or inline. Restrict the file to the server account and launch a CUDA server:
+
+```json
+{
+  "key": "0123456789abcdef",
+  "key_b": "fedcba9876543210",
+  "context_window": 4,
+  "mixing_probability": 0.5,
+  "max_probability": 1.0,
+  "default_enabled": true,
+  "enforce_all": false
+}
+```
+
+```bash
+chmod 600 /run/secrets/sglang-watermark.json
+python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
+  --enable-watermark \
+  --watermark-config /run/secrets/sglang-watermark.json
+```
+
+| Field | Default | Behavior |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `key` | unset | Server key (key A), 1 to 16 hex digits, for requests that enable watermarking without their own key. |
+| `key_b` | unset | Enables dual-key mode with a second server key. Requires `key`. |
+| `context_window` | `4` | Default context window and the maximum that a request may select, from 1 to 64 tokens. |
+| `mixing_probability` | `0.5` | In dual-key mode, the probability of selecting key A for each context. Must be strictly between 0 and 1; a non-default value requires `key_b`. |
+| `max_probability` | `1.0` | Skips watermarking when the largest truncated probability exceeds this value. Must be greater than 0 and at most 1; `1.0` disables the gate. |
+| `default_enabled` | `false` | Watermarks requests that omit the `watermark` field with the server key. Requests may opt out. Requires `key`. |
+| `enforce_all` | `false` | Watermarks requests that omit the `watermark` field and rejects `{"enabled": false}`. Requires `key`. |
+
+Every field is optional and any other field is rejected. The config must be a JSON object of at most 4,096 bytes. A value that starts with `{` is parsed as inline JSON; any other value is read as a path to a regular file, and SGLang logs a warning when that file is readable by group or other users. Inline JSON is visible in the process command line, including `/proc/*/cmdline` on Linux, so pass keys through a file. `--watermark-config` requires `--enable-watermark`. A server key alone does not watermark every request; without `default_enabled` or `enforce_all`, requests must opt in.
+
+SGLang redacts the keys and the `--watermark-config` value from the recorded launch command, startup logs, request logs, server information responses, and request crash-dump payloads. Process and GPU core dumps may contain in-memory keys. Protect those artifacts, the configuration file, and the transport used by clients that send per-request keys.
+
+## Per-request control
+
+The native `/generate` API and the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` APIs accept a `watermark` object with three optional fields:
+
+| Field | Type | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `enabled` | boolean | `true` enables watermarking with the server key; `false` opts out. |
+| `key` | hex string | Watermarks with this key instead of the server key. A key implicitly enables watermarking. |
+| `context_window` | integer | Context window for this request, from 1 to the server's `context_window`. |
+
+On `/generate`, pass `watermark` either at the top level of the request or inside `sampling_params`, but not both; a batched request may pass one object per prompt as a list. On the OpenAI-compatible APIs, pass it as a top-level request field:
+
+```bash
+curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  -d '{
+    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
+    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain photosynthesis."}],
+    "temperature": 1.0,
+    "top_p": 0.95,
+    "return_token_ids": true,
+    "watermark": {"enabled": true, "context_window": 4}
+  }'
+```
+
+The server resolves each request as follows:
+
+| Server mode | No `watermark` field | `{"enabled": false}` | `{"enabled": true}` | `{"key": "HEX"}` |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Watermarking disabled | Off | Off | HTTP 400 | HTTP 400 |
+| `--enable-watermark`, no server key | Off | Off | HTTP 400 | Request key |
+| `--enable-watermark` with a server key | Off | Off | Server key | Request key |
+| Add `default_enabled` | Server key | Off | Server key | Request key |
+| Add `enforce_all` | Server key | HTTP 400 | Server key | Request key |
+
+The request also returns HTTP 400 when:
+
+- the `watermark` object sets neither `enabled` nor `key`, or contains an unknown field;
+- `key` is combined with `"enabled": false`;
+- a key is not 1 to 16 hexadecimal digits;
+- `context_window` is not a positive integer or exceeds the server maximum;
+- a watermarked request uses beam search.
+
+Request-level keys are credentials carried in the request body. Use an authenticated TLS endpoint whenever they cross a host boundary, and avoid recording request bodies in proxies or application logs.
+
+## Dual-key mode
+
+`key_b` in `--watermark-config` applies dual-key selection to every watermarked request. The request's resolved key, whether the server key or a request key, is key A, and the server's second key is key B. A request key therefore replaces key A while key B stays active. Each eligible context uses key A with probability `mixing_probability` and key B otherwise, according to the coin in the [hash contract](#hash-contract); truncation, repeated-context, and greedy rules are unchanged. Without key B, selection uses the single-key path.
+
+A detector holding both keys splits the distinct contexts by the coin, scores each context with its selected key, and tests the union, which is the strongest statistic; it can also test each partition separately. A detector holding only one key can score every distinct context with that key, but the contexts selected for the other key contribute only null samples and dilute the signal.
+
+## Using the detector
+
+`WatermarkDetector` implements the [detection rules](#detection) above. Construct it with the same key, key B, mixing probability, and context window that generation used:
+
+A minimal [reference detection server](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/examples/watermark) exposes the in-tree detector over HTTP and reads keys only from `--watermark-config`.
+
+```python
+WatermarkDetector(
+    key,                      # hex key A
+    *,
+    key_b=None,               # hex key B for dual-key mode
+    mixing_probability=0.5,   # must match the server's mixing_probability
+    context_window=4,         # the request's effective window, 1 to 64
+    max_contexts=4096,        # prefix-test length, 1 to 4096
+)
+```
+
+- `detect_tokens(token_ids, *, prompt_token_ids=())` scores completion token IDs.
+- `detect_text(text, tokenizer, *, prompt_token_ids=())` first encodes the text with `tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)`. Any object with that method works, including Hugging Face tokenizers.
+- `detect(token_ids, *, key, key_b=None, prompt_token_ids=(), mixing_probability=0.5, context_window=4)` is a one-call shortcut.
+
+Token IDs must be unsigned 32-bit integers; any iterable of Python or NumPy integers is accepted.
+
+Every call returns a `WatermarkDetection`:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `combined` | The test to report. Single-key: every distinct context scored with key A. Dual-key: each context scored with its coin-selected key. |
+| `key_a_all_positions` | Every distinct context scored with key A. |
+| `key_b_all_positions`, `key_a_partition`, `key_b_partition` | Dual-key only (`None` otherwise): every context scored with key B, and each coin partition scored with its own key. |
+| `prefix_limit_reached` | `True` when scoring stopped at `max_contexts` distinct contexts. |
+| `tokens_examined` | Completion tokens covered by the test, including repeated and skipped ones. |
+| `repeated_contexts` | Positions skipped because their exact context was already scored. |
+| `skipped_initial_tokens` | Leading completion tokens skipped because no prompt IDs were given. |
+
+Each statistic is a `WatermarkStatistics` with `num_contexts`, `score`, `z_score`, `p_value`, and `log_p_value`.
+
+Prefer the server's token IDs to re-tokenized text, because re-encoding decoded text does not always reproduce the generated IDs. With `"return_token_ids": true`, non-streaming chat completions return `prompt_token_ids` and `response_token_ids` on each choice, and completions return `prompt_token_ids` and `token_ids`.
+
+### In an SGLang environment
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+from sglang.srt.sampling.watermarking import WatermarkDetector
+
+response = requests.post(
+    "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions",
+    json={
+        "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
+        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain photosynthesis."}],
+        "temperature": 1.0,
+        "top_p": 0.95,
+        "return_token_ids": True,
+        "watermark": {"enabled": True},
+    },
+).json()
+choice = response["choices"][0]
+
+detector = WatermarkDetector("0123456789abcdef", context_window=4)
+result = detector.detect_tokens(
+    choice["response_token_ids"],
+    prompt_token_ids=choice["prompt_token_ids"],
+)
+print(result.combined.num_contexts, result.combined.z_score, result.combined.log_p_value)
+```
+
+To score text, pass the model's tokenizer and, when available, the prompt IDs:
+
+```python
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")
+result = detector.detect_text(
+    choice["message"]["content"],
+    tokenizer,
+    prompt_token_ids=choice["prompt_token_ids"],
+)
+```
+
+For a dual-key server, pass both keys and the server's mixing probability:
+
+```python
+detector = WatermarkDetector(
+    "0123456789abcdef",
+    key_b="fedcba9876543210",
+    mixing_probability=0.5,
+    context_window=4,
+)
+result = detector.detect_tokens(completion_ids, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids)
+print(result.combined.p_value, result.key_a_partition.p_value, result.key_b_partition.p_value)
+```
+
+### Standalone, without SGLang or PyTorch
+
+`detector.py` and `config.py` import only the Python standard library and `msgspec`, and the package's `__init__.py` imports only the detector. NumPy arrays are accepted as token-ID iterables, but NumPy is not required. To run detection in a separate application, copy the package directory and install `msgspec`:
+
+```bash
+mkdir -p detector_app
+cp -R python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking detector_app/watermarking
+python -m pip install msgspec
+```
+
+The copy also contains `core.py`, the server runtime, which imports PyTorch; nothing on the detector import path loads it. Run the application with `detector_app` on the import path and import the detector from the copied package:
+
+```python
+from watermarking.detector import WatermarkDetector
+
+single = WatermarkDetector("0123456789abcdef", context_window=4)
+result = single.detect_tokens(completion_ids, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids)
+
+dual = WatermarkDetector("0123456789abcdef", key_b="fedcba9876543210")
+result = dual.detect_tokens(completion_ids, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids)
+```
+
+Text detection needs only an object with `encode(text, *, add_special_tokens)` that returns a list of IDs. For example, with the lightweight `tokenizers` package:
+
+```python
+from tokenizers import Tokenizer
+
+from watermarking.detector import WatermarkDetector
+
+
+class TokenizerAdapter:
+    def __init__(self, name):
+        self._tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
+
+    def encode(self, text, *, add_special_tokens):
+        return self._tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=add_special_tokens).ids
+
+
+detector = WatermarkDetector("0123456789abcdef", context_window=4)
+result = detector.detect_text(text, TokenizerAdapter("Qwen/Qwen3-8B"), prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids)
+```
+
+A detector written from scratch instead of reusing this package must implement the [hash contract](#hash-contract) and all three [detection rules](#detection): prompt alignment, exact-tuple deduplication, and the 4,096-context prefix.

+
+| Feature | Status | Behavior and validation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| CUDA graphs | Verified | Decode graphs, eager fallback, and fused state updates use the same selector contract. |
+| Overlap scheduling | Verified | Prompt initialization is carried with the delayed sampling batch. |
+| Tensor parallelism | Verified | TP2 and TP4 ordinary decode, plus NEXTN with TP2, produce detectable output without rank divergence. |
+| Mixed enabled and disabled requests | Verified | Keys, context windows, histories, and enablement are resolved per request. |

+| Maximum-probability gate | Verified | Positions above `max_probability` use ordinary sampling and do not consume the repeated-context budget. |

+| Decode retraction | Verified | Re-prefill restores the distinct-context history before generation resumes. |

+
+In speculative decoding, verification clones the target logits before forcing, so target-model log-probability computation still sees the pre-watermark distribution. Each draft node gets its own context, rebuilt from its ancestors in the verify tree. Repeated-context admission is conservative across the whole tree: once a context hash appears in an earlier row, later rows with the same hash are not forced, even on sibling branches. This keeps duplicate entries out of the history, but reconvergent wide trees may carry less signal.
+
+## Limitations and performance
+
+- Greedy requests carry no signal, and very low-entropy distributions leave few meaningful alternatives for the selector.
+- A `max_probability` value below 1 keeps ordinary selection at low-entropy positions and can improve speculative draft acceptance, but the unforced positions dilute the detector statistic.
+- Short completions provide few distinct contexts and therefore weak statistical power.
+- Paraphrasing, rewriting, translation, and re-tokenization can weaken or remove the signal.
+- Detection needs the matching key or keys, mixing probability, context window, and tokenizer, and is strongest with the exact prompt token IDs.
+- A request watermarks at most `min(4,096, per-request token-pool capacity)` distinct contexts; later tokens use ordinary sampling.
+- The hashes are MurmurHash3, a keyed but non-cryptographic mix. There is no indistinguishability or unforgeability guarantee, and anyone holding the key can both detect and forge the watermark.
+- Speculative decoding can accept fewer draft tokens when a draft proposal does not match the watermarked target token. The impact depends on tree width and workload.
+- Mixed batches choose the selector path from the batch-wide maximum top-k. A transient unlimited-top-k request can keep that batch on the full-sort path until its sampling metadata is rebuilt.
+- Retraction reconstructs a conservative distinct-context history. Repeated retractions can reduce later signal and add scheduler-side replay work.
+
+On one single-GPU node of each type with public `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, TP1, TRT-LLM MHA, ordinary decoding, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, unlimited top-k, and 800-token sampled outputs, the fused selector measured the following mean output throughput over three repetitions per cell:
+
+| Node | Concurrency | Watermark off | Watermark on | Change |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| GB300 | 1 | 270.25 token/s | 260.44 token/s | -3.63% |
+| GB300 | 8, per stream | 224.88 token/s | 212.84 token/s | -5.35% |
+| B300 | 1 | 258.84 token/s | 247.69 token/s | -4.31% |
+| B300 | 8, per stream | 196.26 token/s | 182.04 token/s | -7.24% |
+
+The GB300 concurrency-eight row was remeasured after the score-precision fix on a default-off server by comparing omitted requests with request-level opt-in. These measurements describe one model, GPU, sampling configuration, and output length. Benchmark your deployment before setting capacity targets. Finite-top-k selector latency at batch size one is also hardware-dependent: in one microbenchmark shape (`top_k=20`), the fast path was 58.8% slower than a full sort on H200 with bfloat16 logits and 6.4% faster on GB300 with float32 logits, and at batch size eight it was faster on both.
+
+On a 2x GB300 node with public `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, TP2, NEXTN 3/1/4, concurrency 8, 1,024-token random inputs, 512-token outputs, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20, the fused speculative path measured the following means over three repetitions:

+| Watermark | Mean TPOT | Aggregate output throughput | Mean accept length |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Off | 2.246 ms | 3,188.9 token/s | 2.759 |
+| On | 2.451 ms | 2,922.2 token/s | 2.783 |

+
+Each speculative row still requires keyed selection, but tree-context reconstruction, repeated-context admission, accepted-context recording, and ring-buffer append run as fused GPU operations. The reported cost remains workload- and acceptance-dependent.

+    tokenizer: Optional[str] = None

+        if (self.text is None) == (self.token_ids is None):
+            raise ValueError("exactly one of text or token_ids is required")
+        return self
+
+

+    p_value: float
+    z_score: float
+    num_contexts: int
+
+

+    watermarked: bool
+    per_key: Optional[dict[str, DetectionStatistics]] = None
+
+

+    return AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(tokenizer_id, trust_remote_code=False)
+
+

+    return DetectionStatistics(
+        p_value=statistics.p_value,
+        z_score=statistics.z_score,
+        num_contexts=statistics.num_contexts,
+    )
+
+
+def per_key_response(
+    result: WatermarkDetection,

+    if result.key_b_all_positions is None:
+        return None
+    return {
+        "key_a_all_positions": statistics_response(result.key_a_all_positions),
+        "key_b_all_positions": statistics_response(result.key_b_all_positions),
+        "key_a_partition": statistics_response(result.key_a_partition),
+        "key_b_partition": statistics_response(result.key_b_partition),
+    }
+
+

+    detector: WatermarkDetector,

+    p_value_threshold: float,
+    default_tokenizer: Optional[str],
+) -> FastAPI:
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    @app.get("/health")
+    def health() -> dict[str, str]:
+        return {"status": "ok"}
+
+    @app.post("/detect")
+    def detect(request: DetectionRequest) -> DetectionResponse:
+        if request.text is not None:
+            tokenizer_id = request.tokenizer or default_tokenizer
+            if tokenizer_id is None:
+                raise HTTPException(
+                    status_code=400,
+                    detail="text detection requires a tokenizer",

+            try:

+                )
+            except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+                raise HTTPException(
+                    status_code=400, detail="failed to load tokenizer"
+                ) from error
+        else:
+            token_ids = request.token_ids
+
+        try:
+            result = detector.detect_tokens(

+    parser.add_argument("--p-value-threshold", type=probability, default=0.01)

+        ),
+        max_contexts=args.max_contexts,
+    )

+        create_app(
+            detector,
+            p_value_threshold=args.p_value_threshold,
+            default_tokenizer=args.tokenizer,
+        ),
+        host=args.host,
+        port=args.port,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main(parse_args())

+@triton.jit
+def _speculative_context_hash_kernel(
+    token_history,
+    lengths,
+    write_positions,
+    req_pool_indices,
+    draft_tokens,
+    custom_mask,
+    positions,
+    context_windows,
+    output_context_hashes,
+    output_context_lengths,
+    context_window: tl.constexpr,
+    draft_token_num: tl.constexpr,
+    FULL_MASK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    request_row = row // draft_token_num
+    draft_position = row % draft_token_num
+    pool_index = tl.load(req_pool_indices + request_row).to(tl.int64)
+    length = tl.load(lengths + pool_index)
+    write_position = tl.load(write_positions + pool_index)
+    requested_window = tl.load(context_windows + request_row)
+    base_length = tl.minimum(length, requested_window)
+    start = tl.where(length == context_window, write_position, 0)
+    source_start = length - base_length
+
+    if FULL_MASK:
+        prefix_length = tl.load(positions + request_row * draft_token_num).to(tl.int64)
+        request_offset = tl.full((), 0, tl.int64)
+        prior_request = 0
+        while prior_request < request_row:
+            prior_prefix_length = tl.load(
+                positions + prior_request * draft_token_num
+            ).to(tl.int64)
+            request_offset += draft_token_num * (prior_prefix_length + draft_token_num)
+            prior_request += 1
+        mask_row_offset = (
+            request_offset
+            + draft_position * (prefix_length + draft_token_num)
+            + prefix_length
+        )
+    else:
+        mask_row_offset = row * draft_token_num
+
+    ancestor_count = 0
+    for candidate in range(1, draft_token_num):
+        ancestor_count += tl.load(custom_mask + mask_row_offset + candidate).to(
+            tl.int32
+        )
+    total_length = base_length + ancestor_count
+    context_length = tl.minimum(total_length, requested_window)
+    skip = total_length - context_length
+
+    state = tl.full((), 0, tl.uint32)
+    rank = 0
+    for candidate in range(context_window):
+        valid = candidate < base_length
+        ring_index = (start + source_start + candidate) % context_window
+        token = tl.load(token_history + pool_index * context_window + ring_index).to(
+            tl.uint32
+        )
+        mixed = murmur3_mix(state, token).to(tl.uint32)
+        state = tl.where(valid & (rank >= skip), mixed, state).to(tl.uint32)
+        rank += valid
+    for candidate in range(1, draft_token_num):
+        valid = tl.load(custom_mask + mask_row_offset + candidate)
+        token = tl.load(draft_tokens + request_row * draft_token_num + candidate).to(
+            tl.uint32
+        )
+        mixed = murmur3_mix(state, token).to(tl.uint32)
+        state = tl.where(valid & (rank >= skip), mixed, state).to(tl.uint32)
+        rank += valid
+
+    context_hash = fmix32(state ^ (context_length * 4).to(tl.uint32))
+    tl.store(output_context_hashes + row, context_hash.to(tl.int64))
+    tl.store(output_context_lengths + row, context_length)

+@triton.jit
+def _speculative_context_eligible_kernel(
+    watermarked_context_hashes,
+    num_watermarked_contexts,
+    req_pool_indices,
+    context_hashes,
+    context_lengths,
+    watermark_enabled,
+    top_ks,
+    output_eligible,
+    draft_token_num: tl.constexpr,
+    max_contexts_per_req: tl.constexpr,
+    HISTORY_BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    request_row = row // draft_token_num
+    draft_position = row % draft_token_num
+    pool_index = tl.load(req_pool_indices + request_row).to(tl.int64)
+    context_hash = tl.load(context_hashes + row).to(tl.int32)
+    count = tl.load(num_watermarked_contexts + pool_index)
+    eligible = (
+        tl.load(watermark_enabled + request_row)
+        & (tl.load(top_ks + request_row) > 1)
+        & (tl.load(context_lengths + row) > 0)
+        & (count < max_contexts_per_req)
+    )
+
+    repeated = False
+    history_offset = 0
+    while (history_offset < count) & eligible:
+        history_positions = history_offset + tl.arange(0, HISTORY_BLOCK_SIZE)
+        history_mask = history_positions < count
+        previous_hashes = tl.load(
+            watermarked_context_hashes
+            + pool_index * max_contexts_per_req
+            + history_positions,
+            mask=history_mask,
+            other=0,
+        )
+        repeated |= tl.sum((previous_hashes == context_hash) & history_mask, axis=0) > 0
+        history_offset += HISTORY_BLOCK_SIZE
+    for prior_position in range(draft_token_num):
+        prior_hash = tl.load(
+            context_hashes + request_row * draft_token_num + prior_position
+        ).to(tl.int32)
+        repeated |= (prior_position < draft_position) & (prior_hash == context_hash)
+    tl.store(output_eligible + row, eligible & ~repeated)

+@triton.jit
+def _watermark_force_partial_argmax_kernel(
+    logits,
+    sorted_probabilities,
+    sorted_token_ids,
+    cumulative_probabilities,
+    context_hashes,
+    eligible,
+    top_ks,
+    top_ps,
+    min_ps,
+    keys,
+    keys_b,
+    mixing_thresholds,
+    partial_scores,
+    partial_token_ids,
+    vocab_size: tl.constexpr,
+    num_splits: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    DUAL_KEY: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    split = tl.program_id(1)
+    ranks = split * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
+    in_bounds = ranks < vocab_size
+    sorted_offsets = row * vocab_size + ranks
+    probabilities = tl.load(
+        sorted_probabilities + sorted_offsets, mask=in_bounds, other=0.0
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    cumulative = tl.load(
+        cumulative_probabilities + sorted_offsets, mask=in_bounds, other=0.0
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    token_ids = tl.load(sorted_token_ids + sorted_offsets, mask=in_bounds, other=0).to(
+        tl.uint32
+    )
+    row_eligible = tl.load(eligible + row)
+    top_k = tl.load(top_ks + row)
+    top_p = tl.load(top_ps + row)
+    min_p = tl.load(min_ps + row)
+    max_probability = tl.load(sorted_probabilities + row * vocab_size).to(tl.float32)
+    is_candidate = (
+        row_eligible
+        & in_bounds
+        & (probabilities > 0.0)
+        & (ranks < top_k)
+        & ((cumulative - probabilities) <= top_p)
+        & (probabilities >= max_probability * min_p)
+    )
+
+    key = tl.load(keys + row).to(tl.uint64)
+    state: tl.uint32 = 0
+    state = murmur3_mix(state, (key & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+    state = murmur3_mix(state, ((key >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+    context_hash = tl.load(context_hashes + row).to(tl.uint32)
+    state = murmur3_mix(state, context_hash)
+    state = murmur3_mix(state, token_ids)
+    hashed = fmix32(state ^ 16)
+    if DUAL_KEY:
+        key_b = tl.load(keys_b + row).to(tl.uint64)
+        mask_state: tl.uint32 = 0
+        mask_state = murmur3_mix(mask_state, (key & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+        mask_state = murmur3_mix(mask_state, ((key >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+        mask_state = murmur3_mix(mask_state, (key_b & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+        mask_state = murmur3_mix(mask_state, ((key_b >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+        mask_state = murmur3_mix(mask_state, context_hash)
+        use_key_a = fmix32(mask_state ^ 20).to(tl.uint64) < tl.load(
+            mixing_thresholds + row
+        ).to(tl.uint64)
+        state_b: tl.uint32 = 0
+        state_b = murmur3_mix(state_b, (key_b & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+        state_b = murmur3_mix(state_b, ((key_b >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32))
+        state_b = murmur3_mix(state_b, context_hash)
+        state_b = murmur3_mix(state_b, token_ids)
+        hashed = tl.where(use_key_a, hashed, fmix32(state_b ^ 16))
+    safe_probabilities = tl.where(is_candidate, probabilities, 1.0)
+    scores = tl.where(
+        is_candidate,
+        _log_uniform_from_hash(hashed) / safe_probabilities,
+        -float("inf"),
+    )
+    local_score = tl.max(scores, axis=0)
+    local_token = tl.min(tl.where(scores == local_score, token_ids, 0xFFFFFFFF), axis=0)
+    output_offset = row * num_splits + split
+    tl.store(partial_scores + output_offset, local_score)
+    tl.store(partial_token_ids + output_offset, local_token.to(tl.int32))
+    tl.store(
+        logits + row * vocab_size + ranks,
+        -float("inf"),
+        mask=row_eligible & in_bounds,
+    )

+@triton.jit
+def _watermark_finalize_and_write_kernel(
+    logits,
+    eligible,
+    partial_scores,
+    partial_token_ids,
+    output_token_ids,
+    vocab_size: tl.constexpr,
+    num_splits: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
+    mask = offsets < num_splits
+    scores = tl.load(
+        partial_scores + row * num_splits + offsets,
+        mask=mask,
+        other=-float("inf"),
+    )
+    max_score = tl.max(scores, axis=0)
+    token_ids = tl.load(
+        partial_token_ids + row * num_splits + offsets, mask=mask, other=-1
+    )
+    token_id = tl.min(
+        tl.where(mask & (scores == max_score), token_ids, 0x7FFFFFFF), axis=0
+    )
+    token_id = tl.where(max_score == -float("inf"), 0, token_id)
+    row_eligible = tl.load(eligible + row)
+    tl.store(logits + row * vocab_size + token_id, 0.0, mask=row_eligible)
+    tl.store(output_token_ids + row, tl.where(row_eligible, token_id, -1))

+def select_watermark_tokens_triton(
+    probabilities: torch.Tensor,
+    context_hashes: torch.Tensor,
+    keys: torch.Tensor,
+    keys_b: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    mixing_thresholds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if probabilities.ndim != 2 or probabilities.dtype != torch.float32:
+        raise ValueError("probabilities must be a 2D float32 tensor")
+    if not probabilities.is_cuda:
+        raise ValueError("Triton watermark selection requires CUDA tensors")
+    batch_size, vocab_size = probabilities.shape
+    if context_hashes.shape != (batch_size,) or context_hashes.dtype != torch.int64:
+        raise ValueError("context_hashes must be int64 with one value per row")
+    if keys.shape != (batch_size,) or keys.dtype != torch.int64:
+        raise ValueError("keys must be int64 with one value per row")
+    if (keys_b is None) != (mixing_thresholds is None):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "dual-key watermark selection requires both key B and mixing thresholds"
+        )
+    dual_key = keys_b is not None
+    if dual_key and (
+        keys_b.shape != (batch_size,)
+        or keys_b.dtype != torch.int64
+        or mixing_thresholds.shape != (batch_size,)
+        or mixing_thresholds.dtype != torch.int64
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("dual-key inputs must be int64 with one value per row")
+    keys_b = keys if keys_b is None else keys_b
+    mixing_thresholds = (
+        context_hashes if mixing_thresholds is None else mixing_thresholds
+    )
+    if not all(
+        tensor.is_cuda and tensor.is_contiguous()
+        for tensor in (probabilities, context_hashes, keys, keys_b, mixing_thresholds)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Triton watermark inputs must be contiguous CUDA tensors")
+
+    output_token_ids = torch.empty(
+        batch_size, dtype=torch.int32, device=probabilities.device
+    )
+    if batch_size == 0:
+        return output_token_ids
+
+    num_splits = triton.cdiv(vocab_size, _BLOCK_SIZE)
+    partial_scores = torch.empty(
+        (batch_size, num_splits), dtype=torch.float32, device=probabilities.device
+    )
+    partial_token_ids = torch.empty(
+        (batch_size, num_splits), dtype=torch.int32, device=probabilities.device
+    )
+    _watermark_partial_argmax_kernel[(batch_size, num_splits)](
+        probabilities,
+        context_hashes,
+        keys,
+        keys_b,
+        mixing_thresholds,
+        partial_scores,
+        partial_token_ids,
+        vocab_size=vocab_size,
+        num_splits=num_splits,
+        BLOCK_SIZE=_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        DUAL_KEY=dual_key,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    _watermark_finalize_argmax_kernel[(batch_size,)](
+        partial_scores,
+        partial_token_ids,
+        output_token_ids,
+        num_splits=num_splits,
+        BLOCK_SIZE=triton.next_power_of_2(num_splits),
+        num_warps=1,
+    )
+    return output_token_ids

+# Text watermarking design
+
+This package implements keyed Aaronson-Gumbel sampling and model-free detection for generated text. Watermarking is opt-in, preserves the target distribution under the ideal hash model, and supports ordinary and speculative decoding. See the [operator guide](../../../../../docs/docs/advanced_features/text_watermarking.mdx) for deployment guidance and the full compatibility matrix.
+
+## Algorithm
+
+After penalties, logit bias, grammar masking, temperature scaling, and top-k/top-p/min-p truncation, let `p[t]` be the probability of token `t`. For each supported token, the selector derives a deterministic uniform `u[t]` from the request key and preceding context, then selects
+
+```text
+argmax_t log(u[t]) / p[t]
+```
+
+This is the logarithmic form of `argmax_t u[t]^(1 / p[t])`. Independent uniform values select each token with probability `p[t]`; masked and truncated tokens have zero support and cannot win. Ties select the lowest token ID.
+
+All hash arithmetic wraps to unsigned 32 bits. `mix` and `fmix32` are the MurmurHash3 x86 32-bit body mix and finalizer:
+
+```text
+mix(state, value):
+  value = value * 0xcc9e2d51
+  value = rotl32(value, 15)
+  value = value * 0x1b873593
+  state = rotl32(state XOR value, 13)
+  return state * 5 + 0xe6546b64
+
+fmix32(value):
+  value = value XOR (value >> 16)
+  value = value * 0x85ebca6b
+  value = value XOR (value >> 13)
+  value = value * 0xc2b2ae35
+  return value XOR (value >> 16)
+```
+
+A key is 1 to 16 hexadecimal digits with an optional `0x` prefix, interpreted as an unsigned 64-bit integer. For context tokens `c_1 ... c_L`, candidate token `t`, and the low and high 32-bit key words:
+
+```text
+context_hash = fmix32(mix(...mix(mix(0, c_1), c_2)..., c_L) XOR (4 * L))
+token_hash   = fmix32(mix(mix(mix(mix(0, key_lo), key_hi), context_hash), t) XOR 16)
+u            = (token_hash + 0.5) / 2^32
+```
+
+The context is the last `h` prompt and committed output tokens before the sampled position. The first generated token therefore uses the prompt tail.
+
+Direct fp32 evaluation of `u` rounds the largest 128 hash values to `1.0`. The Triton and PyTorch selectors preserve relative precision near one by using the direct expression below `2^31` and
+
+```text
+log1p(-(2^32 - token_hash - 0.5) / 2^32)
+```
+
+above it. The integer complement is formed before conversion to floating point.
+
+## Detection
+
+Detection needs token IDs, the same key and context window, and preferably the exact prompt token IDs. For each generated token with uniform value `u`, it adds `-log(1 - u)` to the score. Under the null hypothesis, the sum over `n` contexts follows `Gamma(shape=n, scale=1)`. The detector reports the one-sided upper-tail p-value, its logarithm, and `z = (score - n) / sqrt(n)`.
+
+The detector scores each exact context tuple once. Runtime uses the 32-bit context hash for admission; a rare collision can only add an ordinary null term to detector scoring and dilute the signal. Without prompt IDs, positions whose initial context is unknown are skipped.
+
+Scoring uses a fixed prefix of the first `min(4,096, per-request token-pool capacity)` distinct contexts. Later positions are ordinary samples after runtime reaches the same history budget, so including them would dilute the test. The model-free detector cannot identify entropy-gated or greedy positions; it scores them as conservative null terms.
+
+The [operator guide's detector specification](../../../../../docs/docs/advanced_features/text_watermarking.mdx#detection) is normative for prompt alignment, prefix handling, dual-key partitioning, and result interpretation.
+
+## Runtime design
+
+- **Policy resolution.** Server policy and each request's `watermark` object resolve to a key, context window, and enabled bit before batch construction. Mixed batches retain independent configuration and state per row.
+- **Ring buffer.** Each `req_pool_idx` owns the committed prompt/output tail used to reconstruct contexts. GPU state avoids stale CPU output IDs under overlap scheduling and supplies current contexts for every speculative tree row.
+- **Repeated-context masking.** A context hash is forced at most once per request. Repeated contexts use ordinary sampling, preventing a deterministic short cycle from repeatedly excluding EOS. Only forced contexts enter the history.
+- **Greedy bypass.** Rows normalized to `top_k <= 1`, including `temperature=0`, use ordinary greedy selection and are not recorded.
+- **Entropy gate.** A row uses ordinary sampling when its largest truncated probability exceeds the server's `max_probability`. Skipped contexts remain eligible for a later higher-entropy occurrence.
+- **Speculative decoding.** NGRAM, EAGLE, EAGLE3, and NEXTN reconstruct verify-row contexts from the committed ring tail, tree mask, draft tokens, and positions. Normal decode preserves a clone for logprobs while speculative decode forces a clone, so both report the pre-watermark target distribution. Fused kernels admit contexts and append only accepted tokens.
+- **Selector paths.** Finite `top_k <= 8,192` uses `torch.topk`, canonicalizes boundary ties, and performs small-k truncation. Unlimited top-k retains full-vocabulary sorting. Both paths use the same hash and selection contract.
+- **Disabled-batch exit.** A host-side candidate bit follows filtering and merging. Fully disabled or greedy-only batches skip prompt initialization, verify cloning, selector work, and append kernels.
+- **Retraction and slot reuse.** Re-prefill rebuilds the distinct-context history from accepted output. A new request resets all state for a reused request-pool slot.
+- **Dual key.** A deterministic per-context coin chooses key A with probability `P` and key B otherwise:
+
+  ```text
+  coin      = fmix32(mix(mix(mix(mix(mix(0, a_lo), a_hi), b_lo), b_hi), context_hash) XOR 20)
+  threshold = floor(P * 2^32)
+  key       = key A if coin < threshold else key B
+  ```
+
+  A request key replaces key A; key B remains server-owned. Omitting key B leaves the single-key path unchanged.
+
+## Package layout
+
+| File | Role |
+| --- | --- |
+| `core.py` | Request policy resolution, batch configuration, ring/history state, PyTorch reference selection, and speculative orchestration. |
+| `config.py` | Key parsing, bounded JSON configuration loading, and shared protocol limits. |
+| `detector.py` | Torch-free single-key and dual-key reference detector. |
+| `__init__.py` | Minimal public detector exports. |
+
+The Triton selector and state kernels live in `sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/textseal_selector.py`.
+
+## Server configuration
+
+`--enable-watermark` allocates CUDA watermark state and accepts request configuration. All other settings come from one JSON object passed with `--watermark-config`, as a file path or inline JSON (a value starting with `{`); every field is optional and unknown fields are rejected.
+
+| Field | Default | Behavior |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `key` | unset | Server key A. |
+| `key_b` | unset | Enables dual-key mode with server key B. Requires key A. |
+| `context_window` | `4` | Default context window and per-request maximum, from 1 to 64. |
+| `mixing_probability` | `0.5` | Probability of selecting key A for an eligible context; a non-default value requires `key_b`. |
+| `max_probability` | `1.0` | Uses ordinary sampling when the largest truncated probability exceeds this value. |
+| `default_enabled` | `false` | Uses the server key when a request omits `watermark`; explicit opt-out remains allowed. |
+| `enforce_all` | `false` | Uses the server key by default and rejects explicit opt-out. |
+
+Default-on and enforce-all modes require a server key. A server key without either mode remains available only to requests that opt in.
+
+Use a regular config file readable only by the server account for keys; inline JSON is visible in the process command line. Launch-command, request-log, server-info, and crash-payload rendering redacts key fields and the `--watermark-config` value. Process command lines, client request bodies, and process or GPU core dumps remain separate secret-bearing surfaces.
+
+## Per-request control
+
+The native `/generate` endpoint and OpenAI-compatible completion endpoints accept a `watermark` object:
+
+| Field | Type | Behavior |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `enabled` | boolean | `true` uses the server key; `false` opts out unless enforce-all is active. |
+| `key` | hex string | Replaces key A and implicitly enables watermarking. |
+| `context_window` | integer | Selects a window from 1 through the server maximum. |
+
+| Server mode | Omitted | `{"enabled": false}` | `{"enabled": true}` | `{"key": "HEX"}` |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Watermarking disabled | Off | Off | HTTP 400 | HTTP 400 |
+| Enabled, no server key | Off | Off | HTTP 400 | Request key |
+| Enabled with server key | Off | Off | Server key | Request key |
+| Default-enabled | Server key | Off | Server key | Request key |
+| Enforce-all | Server key | HTTP 400 | Server key | Request key |
+
+A request is rejected when it asks for an unavailable key, combines a key with `enabled=false`, exceeds the server context-window limit, or uses a fail-closed incompatible mode. On `/generate`, place `watermark` at the request top level or in `sampling_params`, not both.
+
+## Using the detector
+
+Within an SGLang environment:
+
+```python
+from sglang.srt.sampling.watermarking import WatermarkDetector
+
+detector = WatermarkDetector("0123456789abcdef", context_window=4)
+result = detector.detect_tokens(completion_ids, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids)
+print(result.combined.num_contexts, result.combined.z_score, result.combined.p_value)
+```
+
+For dual-key output, pass `key_b` and the server's `mixing_probability`. Exact generated token IDs are preferred because decoding and re-tokenizing text need not reproduce the original sequence.
+
+The detector package imports only the Python standard library and `msgspec`; NumPy token arrays are accepted but NumPy is optional. It can be copied into another application without SGLang or PyTorch:
+
+```bash
+cp -R python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking detector_app/watermarking
+python -m pip install msgspec
+```
+
+```python
+from watermarking.detector import WatermarkDetector
+
+detector = WatermarkDetector("0123456789abcdef", context_window=4)
+result = detector.detect_tokens(completion_ids, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids)
+```
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Greedy generation carries no watermark signal. Short and low-entropy text provides less statistical power; the entropy gate trades signal for ordinary sampling at low-entropy positions.
+- Paraphrasing and translation erase the signal. Edits reduce the number of usable contexts.
+- The 32-bit Murmur-derived hash is not a cryptographic PRF. A key holder can detect and forge the watermark.
+- Detection requires the generation key, context window, tokenizer, and preferably the exact prompt and completion token IDs.
+- Generation stops forcing after its context-history budget. Rare 32-bit context-hash collisions and conservative cross-sibling suppression in wide speculative trees can only reduce signal.
+- Unlimited top-k sorts the full vocabulary. Its throughput cost and speculative overhead depend on model, hardware, and workload.
+- Unsupported combinations fail closed. The operator guide maintains the compatibility matrix.
+
+## Attribution
+
+The fused Triton selector is adapted from Meta's [TextSeal](https://github.com/facebookresearch/textseal) selector implementation under Apache-2.0 and reimplemented on the hash contract above. Detection follows this contract rather than TextSeal's detector tooling.

+def _rotl32(value: torch.Tensor, shift: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return ((value << shift) | (value >> (32 - shift))) & _MASK32
+
+
+def _murmur3_mix(state: torch.Tensor, value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    value = (value * 0xCC9E2D51) & _MASK32
+    value = _rotl32(value, 15)
+    value = (value * 0x1B873593) & _MASK32
+    state = state ^ value
+    state = _rotl32(state, 13)
+    return (state * 5 + 0xE6546B64) & _MASK32
+
+
+def _fmix32(value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    value = value ^ (value >> 16)
+    value = (value * 0x85EBCA6B) & _MASK32
+    value = value ^ (value >> 13)
+    value = (value * 0xC2B2AE35) & _MASK32
+    return value ^ (value >> 16)
+
+
+def _as_signed_int32(value: int) -> int:
+    return value if value < (1 << 31) else value - (1 << 32)
+
+
+def _hash_contexts(
+    context_token_ids: torch.Tensor, context_lengths: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    state = torch.zeros(
+        context_token_ids.shape[0], dtype=torch.int64, device=context_token_ids.device
+    )
+    lengths = context_lengths.to(torch.int64)
+    for index in range(context_token_ids.shape[1]):
+        mixed = _murmur3_mix(state, context_token_ids[:, index].to(torch.int64))
+        state = torch.where(index < lengths, mixed, state)
+    return _fmix32(state ^ (lengths * 4))
+
+
+def _watermark_hash32_torch(
+    keys: torch.Tensor, context_hashes: torch.Tensor, token_ids: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    state = torch.zeros(
+        (keys.shape[0], token_ids.shape[0]),
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+        device=keys.device,
+    )
+    keys = keys.view(-1, 1)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, keys & _MASK32)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, (keys >> 32) & _MASK32)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, context_hashes.view(-1, 1) & _MASK32)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, token_ids.view(1, -1) & _MASK32)
+    return _fmix32(state ^ 16)
+
+
+def _dual_key_a_mask_torch(
+    keys_a: torch.Tensor,
+    keys_b: torch.Tensor,
+    context_hashes: torch.Tensor,
+    mixing_thresholds: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    state = torch.zeros_like(keys_a, dtype=torch.int64)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, keys_a & _MASK32)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, (keys_a >> 32) & _MASK32)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, keys_b & _MASK32)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, (keys_b >> 32) & _MASK32)
+    state = _murmur3_mix(state, context_hashes & _MASK32)
+    hashed = _fmix32(state ^ 20)
+    return hashed < mixing_thresholds
+
+
+def _log_uniform_from_hash_torch(hashed: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    lower = torch.log((hashed.to(torch.float32) + 0.5) / _UINT32_SCALE)
+    complement = (_MASK32 - hashed).to(torch.float32) + 0.5
+    upper = torch.log1p(-complement / _UINT32_SCALE)
+    return torch.where(hashed < (1 << 31), lower, upper)
+
+
+def select_watermark_tokens_torch(
+    probabilities: torch.Tensor,
+    context_hashes: torch.Tensor,
+    keys: torch.Tensor,
+    keys_b: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    mixing_thresholds: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if (keys_b is None) != (mixing_thresholds is None):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "dual-key watermark selection requires both key B and mixing thresholds"
+        )
+    token_ids = torch.arange(probabilities.shape[-1], device=probabilities.device)
+    hashed = _watermark_hash32_torch(keys, context_hashes, token_ids)
+    if keys_b is not None:
+        hashed_b = _watermark_hash32_torch(keys_b, context_hashes, token_ids)
+        use_key_a = _dual_key_a_mask_torch(
+            keys, keys_b, context_hashes, mixing_thresholds
+        )
+        hashed = torch.where(use_key_a.view(-1, 1), hashed, hashed_b)
+    scores = torch.where(
+        probabilities > 0,
+        _log_uniform_from_hash_torch(hashed) / probabilities.to(torch.float32),
+        -torch.inf,
+    )
+    return scores.argmax(dim=-1)
+
+
+def _truncate_probabilities(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    temperatures: torch.Tensor,
+    top_ks: torch.Tensor,
+    top_ps: torch.Tensor,
+    min_ps: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    probabilities = torch.softmax(logits / temperatures, dim=-1)
+    sorted_probabilities, sorted_indices = probabilities.sort(dim=-1, descending=True)
+    cumulative_probabilities = torch.cumsum(sorted_probabilities, dim=-1)
+    ranks = torch.arange(logits.shape[-1], device=logits.device).view(1, -1)
+    keep = ranks < top_ks.view(-1, 1)
+    keep &= (cumulative_probabilities - sorted_probabilities) <= top_ps.view(-1, 1)
+    keep &= sorted_probabilities >= (sorted_probabilities[:, :1] * min_ps.view(-1, 1))
+    sorted_probabilities = torch.where(keep, sorted_probabilities, 0.0)
+    sorted_probabilities /= sorted_probabilities.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    return torch.zeros_like(probabilities).scatter_(
+        dim=-1, index=sorted_indices, src=sorted_probabilities
+    )
+
+
+def force_watermark_tokens(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    context_hashes: torch.Tensor,
+    eligible: torch.Tensor,
+    temperatures: torch.Tensor,
+    top_ks: torch.Tensor,
+    top_ps: torch.Tensor,
+    min_ps: torch.Tensor,
+    keys: torch.Tensor,
+    keys_b: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    mixing_thresholds: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    max_top_k: Optional[int] = None,
+    partial_scores: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    partial_token_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    output_token_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    max_probability: float = 1.0,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if logits.is_cuda:
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling.textseal_selector import (
+            force_watermark_tokens_triton,
+        )
+
+        selected = force_watermark_tokens_triton(
+            logits,
+            context_hashes,
+            eligible,
+            temperatures,
+            top_ks,
+            top_ps,
+            min_ps,
+            keys,
+            keys_b,
+            mixing_thresholds,
+            max_top_k=max_top_k,
+            partial_scores=partial_scores,
+            partial_token_ids=partial_token_ids,
+            output_token_ids=output_token_ids,
+            max_probability=max_probability,
+        )
+        return eligible & (selected >= 0)
+
+    probabilities = _truncate_probabilities(
+        logits, temperatures, top_ks, top_ps, min_ps
+    )
+    eligible = eligible & (probabilities.amax(dim=-1) <= max_probability)
+    rows = eligible.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
+    if rows.numel() == 0:
+        return eligible
+    selected = select_watermark_tokens_torch(
+        probabilities[rows].to(torch.float32),
+        context_hashes[rows],
+        keys[rows],
+        keys_b[rows] if keys_b is not None else None,
+        mixing_thresholds[rows] if mixing_thresholds is not None else None,
+    )
+    logits[rows] = -torch.inf
+    logits[rows, selected] = 0.0
+    return eligible

+    def prompt_tails(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> Optional[list[Optional[list[int]]]]:
+        if not batch.forward_mode.is_extend_without_speculative():
+            return None

+            return None

+        has_retracted_request = False
+        for req in batch.reqs:
+            if not req.retracted_stain:
+                histories.append(None)

+            has_retracted_request = True

+        self,
+        req_pool_indices: torch.Tensor,

+        context_hash_history: Optional[Sequence[Optional[Sequence[int]]]] = None,

+            return
+        assert len(prompt_tail_ids) == req_pool_indices.shape[0]

+            index
+            for index, token_ids in enumerate(prompt_tail_ids)
+            if token_ids is not None
+        ]
+        if not valid_positions:
+            return
+

+        batch_positions = torch.tensor(
+            valid_positions, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+        pool_indices = req_pool_indices[batch_positions].to(torch.int64)
+        tails = [list(prompt_tail_ids[index]) for index in valid_positions]
+        lengths = torch.tensor(
+            [len(token_ids) for token_ids in tails], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )

+            [
+                token_ids + [0] * (self.context_window - len(token_ids))
+                for token_ids in tails

+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device=device,

+    def contexts_tail(
+        self,
+        req_pool_indices: torch.Tensor,
+        context_windows: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,

+        pool_indices = req_pool_indices.to(torch.int64)

+        starts = torch.where(lengths == self.context_window, write_positions, 0)
+        offsets = torch.arange(self.context_window, device=self.token_ids.device)
+        gather_indices = (
+            starts.view(-1, 1) + offsets.view(1, -1)
+        ) % self.context_window

+        if context_windows is None:

+            self.context_window, device=self.token_ids.device

+            max=self.context_window - 1
+        )
+        contexts = contexts.gather(1, suffix_indices.to(torch.int64))
+        contexts = torch.where(
+            output_positions < context_lengths.view(-1, 1), contexts, 0
+        )
+        return contexts, context_lengths
